sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s or master’s in mathematics or a related area from an accredited institution; minimum GPA 3.0 in the
last 60 bachelor’s credits or relevant master’s. Linear algebra and advanced calculus are expected
preparation. A completed UChicago mathematics bachelor’s meets the degree-type route; international F-1
applications are eligible. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD in the central application; prepare transcripts, résumé, education/career statement
and three referees. Indicate financial-assistance interest. If using a U.S.-study English exemption, submit the
application and transcript first, then request exemption after allowing up to 72 hours. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
School FAQ permits contacting research faculty and says there is no active list of faculty recruiting RAs. No
prior adviser agreement is a listed application requirement. [s3]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
My ASU tracks application materials and permits resending recommendation requests. Invitations are
described as triggered by referee entry, not as exclusively post-submission. The public FAQ does not establish
post-submission letter revision or reuse. [s3]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Current admissions and fee rules are standing; the department funding flyer is 2025, the central minimum is
2026-27, and Fall 2027 award/commitment terms remain unconfirmed. [s1] [s6] [s8] [s9]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration [Conflict]
School admits for fall only: December 10 for full TA/RA consideration, with rolling admission until July 1. Dates
are standing, not explicitly labeled Fall 2027; time zone unpublished. The central degree page labels July 1
under Summer, which conflicts with the school’s fall-only wording. Use December 10 for funded consideration
and confirm final-term labeling. [s1] [s2]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
School FAQ says all materials should be received by December 10 for funding priority. Later complete files may
be reviewed subject to availability through July 1. No separate letter/score grace period is published. [s1] [s3]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Central minima: TOEFL 80 before January 21, 2026 or revised score 4 thereafter; IELTS Academic 6.5; PTE 60;
Duolingo 105. Scores must normally be within two years of program start. School FAQ mentions TOEFL 100 for
TA applicants; separately, teaching certification is required under the assistant handbook. [s3] [s4] [s10]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Completed U.S. bachelor’s qualifies only through the Other Exemption request form with transcript after
application. An unfinished UChicago degree is not the future-ASU-degree exemption; another route is already
completed 90 semester hours with GPA at least 3.0, or nine U.S. graduate semester hours with GPA 3.0.
Confirm conversion of UChicago units. Admission waivers do not waive spoken-English TA certification. [s4] [s5]
[s10]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
The current school application page says GRE is no longer required and explicitly overrides other pages. The
old FAQ’s required General GRE is superseded; it says Math Subject is not required. Whether optional scores
are evaluated or merely accepted is not specified by the current override. [s1] [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2025 school flyer: USD 26,600 for nine months, approximately 27,000 after qualifiers and 27,400 after
comprehensive exam; USD 5,000 guaranteed fellowship for first summer. Tuition and calendar-year health
insurance covered; about USD 900/year international student fees remain. Central estimated 2026-27
academic-year 50% minimum is USD 26,544. Neither source confirms 2027-28 offer rates. [s8] [s9]
Years of support; Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
TA renewals up to five years depend on satisfactory academic progress and duties. Training is one week in
August; duties average 16-20 hours/week. International students must register at least nine credits each
fall/spring. Admission itself does not guarantee an assistantship. Later summer teaching is limited and
budget-dependent. [s7] [s8]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
School flyer explicitly includes international TAs and their tuition, insurance and enrollment conditions.
Spoken-English certification remains required: 2025 handbook lists SPEAK 55, IELTS speaking 8, TOEFL
speaking 26 or certified ITA training; revised TOEFL-scale equivalents need current confirmation. [s8] [s10]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Request financial aid in the main application; admissions decisions precede assistantship offers. No separate
TA application is described. [s7]
Other funding routes [Prior cycle]
School awards use Scholarship Universe. The published March 4 opening/March 16 deadline applies to 2026-27
awards and includes awards for already enrolled students (e.g., experienced TAs), not a confirmed incoming
Fall 2027 scholarship route. Exact essays, short answers and additional references are portal-specific and
unverified. [s16]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 120 applies to international students studying in the U.S. on F-1 or other nonimmigrant visas. Older USD
115 figures are stale. Pay by Visa or Mastercard; nonrefundable. [s6]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
School application page advertises a limited number of need-based fee waivers; contact graduate mathematics
before paying (grad.math@asu.edu is published on the TA flyer). Exact criteria, form and lead time are not
stated publicly. [s1] [s8]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Jonathan Montaño
Commutative algebra, symbolic powers, determinantal varieties and blowup algebras. [s11] [s13]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Ladder determinantal varieties and their symbolic blowups
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Number theory
Florian Sprung
Iwasawa theory, signed Selmer groups, p-adic L-functions and elliptic curves. [s11] [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 · On the signed Selmer groups for motives at non-ordinary primes in Z_p^2-extensions
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Nancy Childress
Algebraic number theory and p-adic analysis; institutional publication listing is old, so recent activity needs
direct confirmation. [s11] [s14]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2015; latest institutional listing found · On λ-invariants associated to linear extensions of the product
ordering on Nd
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
John Jones
Computational algebraic number theory, number fields and p-adic fields; earlier work on Iwasawa theory and
Artin representations. [a17] [a17p]
Current departmental faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not confirmed publicly.
Research evidence: LuCaNT 2025 proceedings; listed to appear on June 2026 publication list · Families of p-adic fields
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.

Complex geometry
Julien Paupert
Complex hyperbolic geometry, arithmetic lattices, cusps and reflection groups; geometric rather than primarily
algebraic geometry fit. [s11] [s15]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Nil 3-manifolds and cusps of complex hyperbolic surfaces
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
